title: The Scent of Roasted Coffee: A Mother's Sunday
logline: Across fifty years and three generations, an Ethiopian mother's morning coffee ceremony preserves family continuity against displacement and change.
treatment: Through the sensory ritual of the Ethiopian coffee ceremony (Buna Tetu) in Addis Ababa, a grandmother recalls how her mother roasted green beans during the drought in Wollo, proving that tradition is not a static relic, but a daily deliberate act of love.

voice_profile.voice_instruction: Calm, warm, unhurried, intimate elder female cadence with gentle pauses between reflective thoughts.

style_block.visual_style: Kodachrome 64 cinematography, natural diffused morning sunlight, gentle film grain, soft atmospheric smoke, 35mm lens, authentic Ethiopian domestic interiors
style_block.color_palette: Deep amber, terracotta, roasted espresso brown, warm gold, emerald green grass (ketema)
style_block.lighting: Low golden-hour directional light cutting through incense and frankincense smoke

music.title: Memories of the Jebena
music.caption: Acoustic traditional Ethiopian krar and masenqo with gentle washint flute, contemplative tempo, minimalist acoustic drone, warm room reverb, no harsh drums

end_card.text: Made with AI • Antigravity Pipeline • In memory of Emaye

narration.english_translation: In the morning silence, the city of my childhood awakens.
